programme_name: T cell proliferation glycolytic metabolic programme
functional_description: This feature captures actively proliferating T cells with high biosynthetic and glycolytic flux. The signature is dominated by cell cycle machinery (STMN1 for microtubule dynamics), proteasomal processing (PSMA4/5), RNA processing (SNRPG, HNRNPA2B1), actin remodelling (ACTG1, TMSB4X, COTL1), and glycolytic enzyme LDHA. The 43% composition of 'T Proliferating' cells and enrichment of calcium signalling (CALM3) and 14-3-3 adaptor proteins (YWHAQ) indicate rapidly dividing T cells in an anabolic state, likely responding to antigen or cytokine stimulation.
key_evidence: STMN1: canonical proliferation marker controlling microtubule destabilisation during mitosis
PSMA4/PSMA5: proteasomal core subunits essential for protein turnover during rapid cell division
LDHA: glycolytic enzyme diagnostic of Warburg effect in activated T cells
ACTG1/TMSB4X/COTL1: actin cytoskeleton remodelling required for cytokinesis and cell motility
HMGN2: histone-binding protein marking transcriptionally active chromatin during S/G2 phase
suggested_validation: FACS sort top-activating cells and quantify Ki67 co-expression with LDHA/pS6 to confirm proliferation-glycolysis coupling; assess CD4 vs CD8 lineage composition and measure lactate/glucose uptake rate

functional_description: This feature captures an active proliferation and DNA synthesis programme dominated by erythroid progenitors (81.5% of top 200 cells: Pro-Erythroblasts, Polychromatic Erythroblasts, Basophilic Erythroblasts, CFU-E). The signature reflects S/G2-phase cell cycle activity with elevated histone variants (H3F3A, H2AFZ, H2AFY), nucleosome remodelling factors (HMGN2, DEK, HMGB2), and ribonucleoprotein machinery required for rapid ribosome biogenesis and protein synthesis during erythroid maturation.
key_evidence: HMGN2, DEK, HMGB2: DNA-binding chromatin remodellers active in transcriptionally engaged proliferating cells
H3F3A, H2AFZ, H2AFY: Cell cycle-dependent histone variants incorporated during active DNA replication
CKS1B: Cyclin-dependent kinase regulatory protein diagnostic of S/G2-phase cell cycle checkpoint
TUBA1B, TUBB: Tubulin structural proteins required for mitotic spindle assembly in dividing cells
RPS24, TALDO1: Ribosomal and pentose phosphate pathway genes supporting rapid protein synthesis in proliferating erythroblasts
suggested_validation: Perform cell cycle scoring (S/G2-phase markers) and DNA synthesis labelling (BrdU/EdU pulse) on the top 200 activating cells to confirm active cell cycle progression in erythroid progenitors versus quiescent progenitors.

programme_name: B cell identity and antigen presentation programme
functional_description: This feature predominantly captures B cell lineage commitment and maturation, characterized by the coordinated expression of HLA class II antigen presentation machinery (HLA-DRA, HLA-DQB1, HLA-DMA/B, CD74) and B cell-specific transcriptional regulators (CD79A, TCF4, IRF4, SPIB). The top-200 activating cells are overwhelmingly B lineage cells (25% Mature B, 14.5% Small Pre-B, 4.5% Large Pre-B, 4% Immature B, 1.5% Pro-B VDJ) with secondary contributions from professional APCs (pDC 17%, Early ProMono 7%), reflecting shared antigen presentation capacity. The modest T/NK contamination (2.5%) is likely technical noise rather than evidence of a cross-lineage lymphocyte programme.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA, HLA-DQB1, HLA-DMA, HLA-DMB, CD74: HLA class II complex assembly and peptide loading—diagnostic of B cells and professional APCs, not T/NK cells
CD79A: B cell receptor complex component—canonical B lineage marker absent from T/NK differentiation
TCF4, IRF4, SPIB: B cell-specific transcription factors controlling B cell development and plasma cell differentiation
SOX4, TCL1A: Lymphoid progenitor and pre-B cell development factors that drive B lineage commitment
suggested_validation: FACS sorting of top-200 activating cells by CD19+/CD79A+ gating to confirm B cell purity and quantify true T/NK contamination; validate that the T/NK ANOVA rank 3 reflects genuine cross-lineage programme rather than minority cell contamination artefact.

programme_name: Myeloid-intrinsic iron metabolism and lysosomal homeostasis
functional_description: This feature represents a myeloid differentiation and activation programme centered on iron storage (FTH1), polyamine catabolism (SAT1), and lysosomal proteolysis (PSAP, CST3). The programme is dominated by CD16 monocytes, classical monocytes, and dendritic cells—not T/NK cells—reflecting metabolic remodeling during myeloid lineage commitment and antimicrobial effector functions.
key_evidence: FTH1 (rank 1): Ferritin heavy chain diagnostic of iron-storage demand in metabolically active myeloid cells, not lymphocytes
SAT1 (rank 2): Rate-limiting polyamine catabolism enzyme, signature of myeloid activation and antimicrobial oxidative stress response
PSAP (rank 4): Lysosomal sphingolipid activator, indicating enhanced lysosomal degradation capacity in myeloid lineage
SPI1 (rank 9): PU.1 transcription factor master regulator of myeloid and B-lymphoid differentiation—predominantly myeloid context here
TYROBP (rank 8): ITAM-signaling adaptor enriched in monocytes/DCs for pathogen recognition, not T/NK cytotoxicity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of feature-high cells for CD14/CD16 monocyte markers and Prussian blue iron staining to confirm myeloid iron-storage programme, alongside single-cell RNA verification that FTH1/SAT1 co-expression is absent in sorted T/NK cells from the same dataset.

functional_description: This feature marks actively proliferating haematopoietic progenitors undergoing rapid cell division and chromatin remodelling. The signature is dominated by nucleosome-associated proteins (HMGN2, HMGB1/2, H2AFY/Z, PTMA) that facilitate transcriptionally active chromatin, combined with microtubule dynamics (TUBA1B, TUBB, STMN1) and RNA processing machinery (hnRNPs, SRSF3) required for high-throughput protein synthesis during cell cycle progression.
key_evidence: PTMA, HMGN2, HMGB1/2, H2AFY/Z: nucleosome chaperones and chromatin remodellers diagnostic of proliferative states with open chromatin
STMN1, TUBA1B, TUBB: microtubule dynamics and cytoskeletal reorganisation essential for mitotic spindle assembly in dividing cells
HNRNPA1/2B1/A3, SRSF3, PPIA: RNA splicing and protein folding machinery supporting rapid translation during cell cycle
suggested_validation: Flow sort top-activating cells by Ki67/DAPI staining to confirm S/G2M phase enrichment, combined with live-cell imaging of microtubule dynamics using SiR-Tubulin to validate STMN1/tubulin programme activity during mitosis

functional_description: This feature does not represent a shared T/NK lymphocyte programme. The top-200 activating cells are predominantly CD16 monocytes (66.5%) and megakaryocyte precursors, not T cells or NK cells as stated in the context. The gene signature reflects myeloid cell biology: iron storage (FTH1), lysosomal proteases (CTSS, CST3), phagocytic receptors (FCGR3A/CD16), and actin-binding proteins supporting cytoskeletal dynamics in professional phagocytes.
key_evidence: FTH1: ferritin heavy chain for iron storage—diagnostic of iron-handling myeloid cells, not lymphocytes
FCGR3A: CD16 Fc receptor exclusively expressed on monocytes and NK cells; dominance of CD16 Mono (66.5%) indicates myeloid source
CTSS, CST3: lysosomal cysteine proteases essential for phagolysosomal degradation in monocytes, not core lymphocyte machinery
TYROBP: DAP12 adaptor associates with myeloid receptors (CD16, TREM1), not primary NK/T signalling
suggested_validation: Re-examine cell-type composition labelling; if top-200 are genuinely CD16 monocytes, this feature represents myeloid lysosomal/phagocytic programming, not lymphocyte biology. Confirm whether the T/NK ANOVA rank derives from a subpopulation of rare T/NK cells within the top-200 or from contamination in the cell-type annotation.

programme_name: Myeloid innate activation and danger response
functional_description: This feature represents a myeloid-dominant innate immune activation programme characterized by danger-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and antimicrobial responses, NOT a lymphocyte programme. The top 200 cells are 95.5% monocytes and pre-cDCs expressing S100 calcium-binding proteins, ficolin-based pattern recognition, and lysozyme-mediated antimicrobial activity.
key_evidence: S100A9/A8/A6/A4/A11: DAMP-associated calprotectin complex and alarmin signalling diagnostic of activated monocytes/macrophages, not lymphocytes
FCN1: Ficolin pattern recognition receptor for pathogen/DAMP sensing in myeloid cells
LYZ: Lysozyme antimicrobial enzyme housekeeping in monocytes/granulocytes, absent in T/NK cells
TYROBP/FCER1G: Innate immune receptor signalling adaptor proteins in myeloid lineage
LST1: Myeloid differentiation antigen; LST1 actually enhances (not inhibits) myeloid activation despite description
suggested_validation: This is NOT a T/NK lymphocyte feature despite ANOVA ranking. Validate by FACS/multiomics confirmation that feature activation truly correlates with CD8+ T cells or NK cells (CD3+/CD56+), not monocyte markers (CD14/CD11b). Current composition (95.5% monocytes) suggests SAE feature mislabelling or input data contamination.

programme_name: Erythroid haemoglobin synthesis and heme metabolism
functional_description: This feature captures the erythroid differentiation programme centred on haemoglobin production and haem biosynthesis. The signature is dominated by genes encoding globin chains (HBB), haemoglobin assembly chaperones (AHSP), and the complete heme synthetic pathway (UROD, FECH, HMBS). This represents a cell-type-specific erythroid metabolic programme rather than a shared lymphocyte functional module.
key_evidence: HBB: β-globin chain—primary structural component of adult haemoglobin, diagnostic of erythroid differentiation
AHSP: haemoglobin assembly chaperone—essential for preventing toxic free α-globin precipitation during RBC maturation
UROD, FECH, HMBS: heme biosynthetic enzymes—erythroid-specific metabolic commitment pathway
PRDX2, CAT: antioxidant enzymes—protect developing RBCs from haem-iron oxidative stress during erythropoiesis
suggested_validation: Re-examine cell-type annotation: confirm whether reported T/NK cells (top 200 activators) are genuine lymphocytes or misclassified erythroid precursors, as 90% of the feature signature is erythroid-specific with no canonical T/NK or lymphocyte genes present.

functional_description: This feature captures a myeloid-restricted differentiation programme dominated by monocyte and dendritic cell precursors, not a shared T/NK lymphocyte programme. The signature is driven by antimicrobial effectors (LYZ), detoxification enzymes (GSTP1), myeloid transcription factors (SPI1), and innate immune mediators (GRN, AIF1) characteristic of myeloid lineage commitment.
key_evidence: LYZ: lysozyme is a canonical monocyte/macrophage antimicrobial enzyme, not lymphocyte-expressed
SPI1: PU.1 is the master myeloid transcription factor required for monocyte/DC differentiation
GRN: granulin mediator of myeloid activation and inflammation, not T/NK signature
HLA-DMA: antigen presentation molecule highly expressed in professional APCs (DCs, monocytes), not lymphocytes
Cell composition: 50% Pre-cDC + 19% Early ProMono indicates this is fundamentally a myeloid feature, not lymphoid
suggested_validation: Validate that Feature 203 shows high activation in sorted monocyte and dendritic cell populations, not in purified T cells or NK cells from the same atlas, confirming the myeloid identity despite high T/NK ANOVA rank (likely a statistical artifact from global comparison).

functional_description: This feature captures active erythroid maturation characterized by heme biosynthesis (UROD, BLVRB), iron metabolism (FTH1), and oxidative stress management (PRDX2). The programme is driven by erythroid lineage commitment rather than a shared T/NK lymphocyte programme, despite the initial ranking suggesting T/NK enrichment.
key_evidence: UROD & BLVRB: heme biosynthetic pathway enzymes diagnostic of erythroid differentiation
FTH1: iron storage critical for haemoglobin synthesis in polychromatic/basophilic erythroblasts
PRDX2: antioxidant defence against ROS generated during intense haem/globin synthesis
TUBA1B/TUBB: cytoskeletal proteins supporting morphological changes during erythroid maturation
suggested_validation: Validate feature composition: re-examine top 200 activating cells to confirm if true lymphocyte enrichment exists; if predominantly erythroid, this represents a feature mislabeled as T/NK and warrants SAE retraining or feature reassignment to erythroid lineage programmes.

functional_description: This feature represents active ribosomal biogenesis and protein synthesis machinery characteristic of erythroid progenitors (CFU-E, Pro-Erythroblasts, BFU-E) undergoing rapid proliferation and haemoglobin production. The dominant ribosomal protein genes (RPS/RPL family) and translation factors reflect the extraordinary translational demands of erythroid differentiation, which requires massive haemoglobin synthesis.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPL7A, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0: collectively encode core 40S and 60S ribosomal subunits essential for ribosome assembly during rapid protein synthesis
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor enabling high-throughput protein synthesis capacity required for haemoglobin production
STMN1: microtubule dynamics regulator supporting cell cycle progression in proliferating erythroid progenitors
LDHB: glycolytic enzyme supporting energy demands of protein synthesis in metabolically active progenitors
suggested_validation: This is NOT a T/NK lymphocyte programme—the feature is dominated by erythroid cells (77% CFU-E/Pro-Erythroblast/BFU-E). Validate by flow cytometry sorting CD34+CD71+ erythroid progenitors and confirm ribosomal protein expression by qPCR or proteomics; compare to mature RBCs and T/NK populations to confirm erythroid-lineage specificity rather than shared lymphocyte biology.

programme_name: ANNOTATION ERROR: Not a lymphocyte programme
functional_description: This feature does not represent a shared T/NK lymphocyte programme. The top 200 activating cells are predominantly dendritic cells (62% cDC1, 13% cDC2, 19.5% Pre-cDC) and megakaryocyte precursors, NOT T cells or NK cells. The gene signature is diagnostic of professional antigen-presenting cells: HLA class II molecules (HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1, HLA-DQA1, HLA-DQB1, HLA-DMA, HLA-DMB) and CD74 (invariant chain required for MHC-II trafficking). This is the hallmark of the dendritic cell/APC compartment, not lymphocyte biology.
key_evidence: CD74 + HLA class II genes (DRA, DRB1, DPA1, DPB1, DQA1, DQB1, DMA, DMB): diagnostic of MHC-II+ professional APCs, absent in mature T/NK cells
Cell composition mismatch: 94.5% of top cells are cDC1/cDC2/Pre-cDC; the stated T/NK ANOVA rank appears to be a data annotation error
SPI1 (PU.1) and AIF1: myeloid/dendritic cell differentiation factors, not lymphocyte programmes
suggested_validation: Verify cell-type annotation pipeline: manually validate cDC1/Pre-cDC/cDC2 assignments in top 200 activating cells using flow cytometry markers (CD11c, CD141, CD1c) and re-examine whether T/NK ANOVA ranking reflects actual cell composition or classification error

programme_name: Myeloid metabolic priming and stress response
functional_description: This feature reflects a metabolic and proteostatic programme dominated by myeloid cells (cDC1/Pre-cDC/MKP) rather than T/NK lymphocytes. The signature is characterized by elevated oxidative phosphorylation (COX5A, VDAC1, SLC25A5), glycolytic capacity (LDHA, ENO1), and cellular stress management (GSTP1, ATG3, AIF1). The minimal T/NK contribution (1.5% T Proliferating only) indicates this is not a true lymphocyte-intrinsic programme.
key_evidence: GSTP1, VDAC1, SLC25A5: Antioxidant and mitochondrial metabolic markers characteristic of metabolically active myeloid cells (cDC1 >40% of top 200)
COX5A, LDHA, ENO1, PPA1: OXPHOS and glycolytic enzymes indicating bioenergetic priming typical of antigen-presenting cells rather than resting lymphocytes
ATG3, AIF1: Autophagy and stress-response machinery—elevated in professionally phagocytic/antigen-presenting cells, not T/NK lymphocyte-specific programmes
suggested_validation: Validate that T/NK cells in top activators are genuinely T Proliferating vs. mislabeled by sorting top 200 cells and performing flow cytometry with lineage markers (CD3, CD56, CD33, CD11c); re-examine whether this is a technical artifact or genuine myeloid-driven feature misclassified as lymphoid.

functional_description: This feature represents a programme of active nucleocytoplasmic trafficking and pre-mRNA splicing machinery, driven by high expression of nuclear import factors (RANBP1), splicing regulators (SRSF2, SRSF3, SNRPB), and chromatin remodelers (HMGB1, DEK). The mixed cell-type composition (predominantly erythroblasts and megakaryocyte precursors with minor T/NK representation) suggests this is fundamentally a haematopoietic progenitor state rather than a lymphocyte-specific programme.
key_evidence: RANBP1: nucleocytoplasmic transport machinery; diagnostic of active nuclear import during proliferation
SRSF2/SRSF3: SR-rich pre-mRNA splicing factors; hallmark of transcriptionally active cycling cells
HMGB1: chromatin architecture protein; elevated in proliferating progenitors requiring dynamic transcription
DEK: DNA-binding protein involved in transcriptional regulation; associated with chromatin remodeling in cycling cells
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sorting by RANBP1/SRSF2 protein expression combined with Ki67 staining to confirm this marks proliferating haematopoietic progenitors rather than a T/NK cell-specific programme, given the erythroblast and megakaryocyte dominance contradicts the stated T/NK lymphocyte focus.

functional_description: This feature captures the erythroid differentiation programme dominated by haemoglobin chain production (HBA1, HBA2, HBB) and mitochondrial haem biosynthesis machinery (ALAS2, FECH, SLC25A37). The programme integrates iron transport, oxidative stress management (CAT), and protein quality control (AHSP chaperone function) essential for coordinated globin chain assembly during erythrocyte maturation.
key_evidence: HBA1/HBA2/HBB: Alpha and beta globin chains—core structural proteins of haemoglobin, diagnostic of erythroid lineage commitment
ALAS2: Erythroid-specific mitochondrial enzyme catalysing first committed step of haem biosynthesis—rate-limiting for haemoglobin production
FECH: Ferrochelatase catalysing final step of haem synthesis (iron insertion into protoporphyrin)—essential for functional haemoglobin assembly
SLC25A37: Mitochondrial iron importer required for haem biosynthesis—links iron metabolism to erythroid differentiation
AHSP: Haemoglobin assembly chaperone preventing toxic free alpha-globin precipitation—protective quality control during maturation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for CD71 (transferrin receptor) and haemoglobin content across erythroid developmental stages (Pro-E, Basophilic-E, Polychromatic-E, Orthochromatic-E) to confirm feature activation correlates with progressive haem and globin accumulation during terminal erythroid maturation.

functional_description: This feature does not represent a lymphocyte programme. The top 200 activating cells are 85.5% erythroid precursors (basophilic, polychromatic, pro- and orthochromatic erythroblasts) and megakaryocyte precursors. The gene signature reflects intensive ribosomal protein synthesis (RPS17, RPS24, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPLP0), RNA processing (SNRPG, SRSF3, SLBP), and nucleotide binding proteins (YBX1, HMGB1) characteristic of actively differentiating haematopoietic precursors undergoing rapid protein synthesis and organelle biogenesis.
key_evidence: RPS17, RPS24, RPL37A: Ribosomal proteins diagnostic of high translation demand in erythroid precursors
SLBP: Histone mRNA-binding protein specific to replication-dependent histone synthesis in S-phase erythroid cells
YBX1, HMGB1: RNA chaperones and nucleic acid binding proteins supporting active transcription/translation during erythroid differentiation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometric validation confirming feature activation in CD71+/CD235a+ erythroid precursors and CD41+ megakaryocytes rather than T cells/NK cells; re-examine SAE training data for potential mislabeling of non-lymphoid cells in top activating population

functional_description: This feature does not represent a shared lymphocyte programme. The top 200 'activating' cells are 93.5% erythroid precursors (Pro-Erythroblasts and Basophilic Erythroblasts), with only background lymphocyte contamination. The signature reflects active erythropoiesis: mitochondrial electron transport (MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-CO2) supporting haemoglobin synthesis, intensive protein translation (ribosomal proteins), and iron metabolism (FTH1) essential for erythroid differentiation.
key_evidence: MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-CO2: mitochondrial OXPHOS genes diagnostic of high-demand erythroid haemoglobin synthesis, not lymphocyte-specific
RPS genes + EEF1B2 + RPLP0: translation machinery reflecting massive ribosome burden in actively synthesising erythroblasts, not lymphocyte signature
FTH1: ferritin heavy chain essential for iron storage in erythropoiesis, absent in T/NK cell activation programmes
suggested_validation: Verify the T/NK ANOVA rank reflects data annotation error: manually inspect SAE latent space to confirm whether lymphocytes genuinely co-activate with this feature, or whether this is mislabelled erythroid-specific feature that incidentally ranks high in T/NK comparison due to statistical artefact

functional_description: This feature represents the erythroid lineage differentiation programme, NOT a lymphocyte-specific functional programme. The top-200 activating cells are 93% erythroblasts at various maturation stages, characterised by haemoglobin chain synthesis (HBB, HBA1/2), erythroid-specific haem biosynthesis (ALAS2, FECH), and membrane protein organisation (EPB42, SLC4A1, AHSP). This is a lineage-specific rather than cross-lineage programme.
key_evidence: HBB, HBA1, HBA2: Diagnostic adult haemoglobin chains - exclusive erythroid expression
ALAS2: Erythroid-specific mitochondrial enzyme for haem synthesis initiation
AHSP: Alpha-globin chaperone - essential for safe haemoglobin assembly in maturing erythrocytes
EPB42, SLC4A1: Erythrocyte membrane proteins - structural determinants of RBC maturation
suggested_validation: The annotated feature is MISLABELED as T/NK ANOVA rank 18: verify SAE training labels and confirm that the top-200 activating cells are genuinely 93% erythroblasts rather than lymphocytes. If confirmed erythroid, reclassify as an erythroid maturation feature rather than a lymphocyte programme.

functional_description: This feature represents a high-biosynthetic-demand programme enriched in early erythroid and megakaryocytic precursors characterized by massive ribosomal protein expression, active mRNA splicing, and oxidative phosphorylation. The programme reflects the extreme protein synthesis capacity required for rapid haemoglobin production (erythroblasts) and platelet protein synthesis (megakaryocytes), rather than a lymphocyte-specific programme.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPLP0: Ribosomal structural proteins; diagnostic of high translation demand in erythropoiesis and megakaryopoiesis
SRSF2, SRSF3, SNRPB: SR-rich splicing factors; required for high-throughput mRNA processing in biosynthetically active cells
COX5A, SLC25A3: Oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial phosphate transport; erythroid and megakaryocytic precursors require ATP for biosynthesis
PTMA, YBX1, HNRNPC: RNA-binding proteins stabilizing transcripts during active protein synthesis
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry with CD34, CD41, CD71 markers to confirm the feature activates specifically in megakaryocyte/erythroid precursors rather than T/NK cells; if T/NK composition is artefactual, re-examine data for annotation errors.

functional_description: This feature captures the core erythroid differentiation programme characterized by iron metabolism, heme synthesis, and hemoglobin assembly. The signature reflects the metabolic and biosynthetic demands of erythropoiesis, from pro-erythroblast through polychromatic stages, including iron storage (FTH1), heme degradation (BLVRB), and alpha-globin chaperone assistance (AHSP).
key_evidence: FTH1: ferritin heavy chain for iron sequestration, critical for heme biosynthesis precursor availability
BLVRB: biliverdin reductase completing final step of heme catabolism, diagnostic of erythroid maturation
AHSP: alpha-globin stabilization chaperone essential for hemoglobin tetramer assembly
GYPC: glycophorin C, erythroid-restricted membrane glycoprotein marking mature RBC identity
HMGB2/HMGN2: nucleoid-associated proteins regulating chromatin state during erythroid transcriptional reprogramming
PRDX2 & IDH2: antioxidant and mitochondrial metabolism supporting intense heme synthesis
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sorting on CD71 (transferrin receptor) and CD235a (glycophorin A) to confirm erythroid-specific feature activation is enriched in pro-, early basophilic, and polychromatic erythroblasts relative to other haematopoietic populations

functional_description: This feature captures a shared programme of active protein synthesis and nucleocytoplasmic transport in rapidly proliferating lymphoid progenitors. The signature combines nuclear RNA processing machinery (hnRNPs, PTMA), mitochondrial carriers (SLC25A3, SLC25A5), and molecular chaperones (PPIA) essential for sustaining high metabolic demand during cell division and differentiation.
key_evidence: PTMA: Anti-apoptotic nucleolar/nuclear protein essential for cell survival during proliferation phases
HNRNPA1/A2B1/A3/C: RNA binding proteins coordinating mRNA splicing and export during rapid protein synthesis
SLC25A3/SLC25A5: Mitochondrial phosphate and ADP/ATP transporters supporting energy metabolism in dividing cells
PPIA: Peptidylprolyl isomerase enabling nascent protein folding during translation surge
HMGB1/HMGN2: Chromatin-associated proteins marking transcriptionally active, proliferation-ready nuclei
suggested_validation: Co-stain cycling T cells and NK cells with BrdU incorporation + TMRM (mitochondrial membrane potential) + RNA-FISH for hnRNP localization to confirm synchronous nucleocytoplasmic and mitochondrial biosynthetic engagement during G1/S transition

functional_description: This feature represents the erythroid developmental programme characterized by haemoglobin synthesis, haem biosynthesis, and oxidative stress management. The top-200 activating cells are predominantly polychromatic and basophilic erythroblasts undergoing terminal differentiation with massive accumulation of globin chains and haem groups. This is NOT a lymphocyte programme.
key_evidence: HBB: Beta-globin chain, core component of haemoglobin tetramers diagnostic of erythroid differentiation
AHSP: Alpha-globin specific chaperone essential for preventing free alpha-globin precipitation during haemoglobin assembly
FECH: Ferrochelatase catalyses final step of haem synthesis (protoporphyrin IX → haem), critical for functional haemoglobin
suggested_validation: CRITICAL ISSUE: This feature does NOT represent a T/NK lymphocyte programme. The reported T/NK ANOVA rank of 22 appears erroneous—the top-200 activating cells are 90.5% erythroblasts with zero T or NK cells. Validate SAE feature composition using flow cytometry or immunophenotyping to confirm cell-type assignment, as this feature signature is incompatible with lymphocyte biology.

functional_description: This feature does not represent a lymphocyte programme. The top 200 activating cells are 86% erythroblasts at various differentiation stages, with gene signatures dominated by hemoglobin chains (HBB, HBA1), erythroid-specific heme synthesis enzymes (ALAS2, FECH), and red blood cell membrane proteins (EPB42, BSG). The 2% contamination with plasma cells and megakaryocytes reflects normal bone marrow heterogeneity.
key_evidence: HBB/HBA1: hallmark adult hemoglobin chains diagnostic of erythroid lineage, not lymphocytes
ALAS2/FECH: erythroid-specific mitochondrial enzymes for heme biosynthesis, absent in T/NK cells
EPB42/AHSP: erythrocyte membrane proteins and alpha-globin chaperone, erythroid-restricted
suggested_validation: Verify SAE training data stratification—this feature appears mislabeled as T/NK-enriched; re-examine cell-type annotation pipeline for erythroblast misclassification in lymphocyte gates.

programme_name: Erythroid iron metabolism and protein synthesis
functional_description: This feature captures a specialized metabolic programme of erythroid precursors characterized by intense iron storage (FTH1-mediated ferritin synthesis) and elevated ribosomal protein expression to support massive haemoglobin synthesis. The programme reflects the extraordinary biosynthetic demand of erythropoiesis, where iron homeostasis and translational capacity are tightly coordinated to enable the production of >280 million RBCs daily.
key_evidence: FTH1: Heavy chain ferritin essential for iron sequestration and detoxification in iron-replete erythroblasts undergoing Hb synthesis
RPS2/RPL4/RPL7A/RPS17/RPS24/RPL37A: Coordinate ribosomal protein elevation drives translational machinery expansion required for sustained globin chain synthesis
MT-CO3: Oxidoreduction and electron transfer reflect mitochondrial density in basophilic erythroblasts supporting haem synthesis energy demands
YBX1: RNA-binding protein facilitates mRNA stability and translation during high-flux haemoglobin production
PRDX2: Antioxidant machinery protects against ROS generated by intense iron metabolism and mitochondrial activity
suggested_validation: FISH or immunofluorescence co-staining of FTH1 with erythroid markers (CD71/TfR1) and quantitative assessment of ribosomal protein content across erythroid differentiation stages (proerythroblast→polychromatic→orthochromatic) to confirm iron-synthesis coupling

programme_name: Erythroid mitochondrial biogenesis and protein synthesis
functional_description: This feature captures the metabolic programme of early-stage erythroid differentiation, dominated by oxidative phosphorylation machinery and ribosomal protein synthesis. The top 200 activating cells are predominantly pro-erythroblasts and CFU-E cells, which require massive mitochondrial capacity and protein synthetic machinery for haemoglobin production and organellar biogenesis prior to enucleation.
key_evidence: MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND1, MT-ND5, UQCRH, UQCRQ, NDUFS5: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation complexes I, III, and IV—essential for ATP generation supporting erythroid proliferation and haemoglobin synthesis
RPL37A, RPS24, RPS23, RPLP0, RPL7A, RPS17: Ribosomal structural proteins required for sustained translation at levels necessary for erythroid differentiation
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic factor critical for erythroid progenitor survival during differentiation; S100A6: calcium-buffering protein supporting metabolic regulation in metabolically active erythroblasts
suggested_validation: FACS-sort pro-erythroblasts vs. mature erythrocytes and perform oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and protein synthesis assays; validate feature activation does not co-occur with T/NK-specific markers (CD8, NKG7, GNLY)

functional_description: This feature does not represent a shared lymphocyte programme. The top 200 activating cells are predominantly erythroblasts (95.5%) and megakaryocyte precursors, with negligible lymphocyte content (1% plasma cells). The gene signature is dominated by erythroid-specific haemoglobin genes (HBA1, HBA2, HBB), haem biosynthesis (ALAS2), and mitochondrial metabolism supporting red blood cell maturation.
key_evidence: HBA1/HBA2/HBB: Erythroid-lineage specific globin chains diagnostic of haemoglobin production
ALAS2: Erythroid-specific mitochondrial enzyme for haem synthesis, not expressed in lymphocytes
BPGM: 2,3-DPG metabolism specific to mature red blood cells
Cell composition: 95.5% erythroblasts/megakaryocytes, contradicts T/NK classification

functional_description: This feature captures the core erythroid maturation programme, characterized by intense hemoglobin synthesis, heme metabolism, and iron homeostasis. The signature reflects progressive differentiation from pro-erythroblasts through polychromatic erythroblasts, marked by massive ribosomal protein expression supporting globin chain synthesis and coordinated upregulation of heme biosynthetic enzymes and iron storage proteins.
key_evidence: HBB: Direct beta-globin synthesis, the primary protein cargo of maturing erythroid cells
BLVRB: Final step in heme degradation/metabolism, essential cofactor for hemoglobin function
AHSP: Alpha-globin chaperone ensuring proper hemoglobin assembly and preventing toxic free alpha-globin
FTH1: Iron storage protein critical for supporting high iron demand during hemoglobinization
RPS17, RPLP0, RPS24, RPL7A: Ribosomal proteins enabling extraordinary translational capacity for globin synthesis
PRDX2: Antioxidant protection against reactive oxygen species from heme and iron metabolism
suggested_validation: This feature does not represent a T/NK lymphocyte programme despite the ANOVA ranking. Re-evaluate the annotation: confirm cell-type classification of top-200 activating cells using flow cytometry or transcriptomic markers (CD3, CD56, CD71, CD34) as the 100% erythroid cell composition indicates possible mislabeling or contamination in the original annotation.

functional_description: This feature represents the late-stage erythroid differentiation programme, characterized by massive haemoglobin production (HBB, HBA1, HBA2) and iron-dependent haem biosynthesis (ALAS2, FECH). The top-200 activating cells are overwhelmingly erythroblasts (97% of composition), not T/NK cells as stated in the context.
key_evidence: HBB, HBA1, HBA2: Adult haemoglobin subunit genes - hallmark of orthochromatic and polychromatic erythroblasts
ALAS2: Erythroid-specific δ-aminolevulinic acid synthase - commits to haem synthesis pathway in mitochondria
FECH: Ferrochelatase - final enzyme inserting Fe2+ into protoporphyrin IX, completing haem biosynthesis
SLC25A39: Mitochondrial transporter - likely involved in iron/metabolite import for haem synthesis
SNCA, UBB, FBXO7: Protein quality control - manage massive translational load and organellar remodelling during erythroid maturation
